SHAPE COLORING FUN · TODDLER 3 · AGE 2

Color the Tall Rectangle

A stretched-up rectangle — like a tower!

THE PICTURE — COLOR RIGHT ON IT

Your picture is ready.

Pick a crayon, then color straight on the picture with your finger, a stylus or the mouse. Press Save my work when you are proud — your colors stay here for next time, and the picture is yours to keep.

← RectanglePrevious coloring pageRectangle & Bus →Next coloring page
HOW TO DO IT

Three little steps.

  1. 1

    Reach up

    This rectangle stands tall like a tower — stretch up with it!

  2. 2

    Color it

    Color top to bottom, like rain running down a window.

  3. 3

    Compare

    The first rectangle lay down; this one stands up!

Ask a grown-up to read the steps aloud the first time. After that, you know just what to do.

YOUR PENCIL CASE

Pick your tools.

Pencil, nine crayons, an eraser, undo, redo and clear — the tools appear right here and work on the picture. Save keeps your finished art and remembers it for next time.

MY PROGRESS

Save it to keep it.

This page is cleared for you the moment you save your finished picture. Nothing counts until then — opening the page is just opening the door.

Cleared! Your colored picture is saved on this device for your child, and the ribbon is on in Class 9. Come back any time — your colors will be waiting.

SHARE THIS ACTIVITY

Pass it on.

XFacebookWhatsApp

Share buttons open in a new tab. The copy button copies this page’s address — nothing is tracked.

PREFER PAPER?

Print the twin.

The same picture lives in the Coloring Pages library with its download and print buttons: /coloring-pages/shapes/tall-rectangle/. Crayons beat styluses sometimes.

FOR GROWN-UPS

What this page practises.

Lying down or standing up — same shape, different mood. Two-year-olds love flipping the words: stand tall like the rectangle, lie flat like the other one.

  • Tall and short
  • Shape naming
  • Top-to-bottom strokes
  • Comparing shapes

This activity belongs to Class 9 — Colors and Shapes (Age 2) on the Learning Path, and the printable twin lives in Coloring Pages — Shapes. Progress is saved on this device for the child chosen in My Classroom — and only a real save of finished work marks it cleared, never just opening the page.
